chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

It is not befitting that you pray the two cycles of the obligatory Tawaf except near the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). As for the optional (prayers), then (pray) wherever you wish from the Masjid.

key_terms.التَّطَوُّعُ: Optional or voluntary acts of worship
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two cycles of prayer performed during the obligatory circumambulation
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Standing Place of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)

ai.seo_question: Where should one pray the two cycles of Tawaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the juristic distinction between the obligatory and voluntary two-rak'ah prayers of Tawaf, anchoring the former specifically at the Maqam Ibrahim as a site of prophetic legacy. Shia scholars emphasize this location to preserve the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams, while allowing flexibility for voluntary prayers elsewhere in the Haram to accommodate varying levels of devotion and crowd conditions.
